item.title: Systematic mapping of enhancers, silencers, and topological elements with prime editing deletion screens.
item.abstract: Noncoding regulatory elements in the human genome can control gene expression through distinct mechanisms, including acting as enhancers, silencers, or topological elements. However, we lack tools to identify all such classes systematically and quantify their effects on gene expression in an endogenous genomic context. Here we develop Swap-seq, a method that combines pooled twin prime editing with flow-sorting to delete hundreds of endogenous regulatory sequences and measure their quantitative effects on the expression of a nearby gene. We apply Swap-seq to dissect the regulatory elements that control PPIF expression in THP-1 monocytes. We quantify the effects of distal and intronic enhancers, characterize CTCF insulators, and discover a silencer that regulates distal genes through histone deacetylase (HDAC)-mediated repression of neighboring enhancers. Hundreds of other genomic elements share its chromatin signatures and transcription factor binding sites, suggesting that this silencer represents a broader class of repressive elements. We leverage Swap-seq data to benchmark sequence-to-function models and show that they often capture the local activity of regulatory elements but fail to link them to distal target genes. Swap-seq thus provides a generalizable tool to discover regulatory elements across mechanistic classes, characterize their effects on gene expression, and generate large-scale datasets for evaluating sequence-to-function models.

item.title: Programming N-linked glycan composition through de novo protein design.
item.abstract: N-linked glycans are ubiquitous post-translational modifications that mediate diverse biological processes, including cell signaling and adhesion, molecular recognition, and host-pathogen interactions. Despite their importance, N-linked glycans have largely remained beyond the reach of biomolecular design due to a lack of methods capable of jointly modeling glycans and protein structure. Here, we develop a general all-atom computational pipeline for creating de novo glycoproteins in which the amino acid sequence encodes both the location and composition of N-linked glycans. The method uses three-dimensional protein structure to tune glycan accessibility to processing enzymes in the eukaryotic secretory pathway. Systematic increases in steric restriction progressively reduced processing, shifting glycans from heterogeneous complex-type structures toward increasingly underprocessed oligomannose-type species resembling those found on many viral glycoproteins. Despite this programmed restriction, the resulting oligomannose glycans remained accessible for biological recognition, inhibiting uropathogenic Escherichia coli adhesion to human bladder cells and binding mannose-binding lectin. These results establish steric control of N-glycan processing as a genetically encodable design principle and extend computational protein design to functional glycoproteins with programmed composition.

item.title: Synthetic biology for heritable viral disease resistance in livestock.
item.abstract: Synthetic biology is rapidly expanding the strategies available to engineer disease resistance in livestock. Genome editing of host factors required for pathogen entry or replication has generated complete or partial resistance in pigs, cattle, and chickens, culminating in the first regulatory approvals of PRRSV-resistant pigs. Another frontier is emerging in which synthetic antiviral circuits detect and suppress infection through programmable molecular responses. Precision editing tools, including base and prime editors, may enable resistance through smaller and more targeted genomic changes, while organoid and stem cell-derived cell cultures are accelerating pre-animal validation. This review examines recent advances in host-factor engineering, synthetic antiviral systems, and enabling platforms, and considers the challenges of commercial dissemination, regulation, and public acceptance. Together, these developments position engineered resistance as a potentially important component of integrated livestock disease control.

item.title: Minimal indel-inducing and window-adjustable base editing using inactive Cas12b effectors.
item.abstract: The recent CRISPR-Cas12b gene editing system, which recognizes DNA targets based on reprogrammed RNA, is increasingly being utilized in various fields. We developed an advanced base-editing technology that seamlessly integrates the TadA8e deaminase with an inactivated dBhCas12b (dead Bacillus hisashii Cas12b) module, enabling precise single-base DNA substitutions in human cell lines. Using the TadA8e-dBhCas12b module, we successfully induced single-base (A-to-G) substitutions at genomic target sites in HEK293FT cells, with an efficiency ranging from 3.96% ± 1.10%-25.78% ± 0.78%, with minimal unintended indel formation due to target DNA nicking. Notably, the editing window of the TadA8e-dBhCas12b module, spanning approximately positions 5-10, can be precisely modulated through the introduction of point mutations within the RuvC domain and the fusion of nonspecific DNA-binding domains, such as Sso7d. These modifications enable efficient base editing at target sites containing thymine-rich protospacer-adjacent motifs (PAMs). The optimized TadA8e-dBhCas12b platform therefore represents a complementary alternative to conventional CRISPR-Cas9-derived base editors and may broaden the range of targetable pathogenic variants, particularly those located within T-rich genomic contexts. Its DNA context-dependent editing window and expanded targeting capacity highlight its potential utility in both basic biological research and therapeutic genome editing.

item.title: Plug-and-Play or Plug-and-Pray? Impact of random versus targeted integration on the linearity and orthogonality of synthetic gene circuits in CHO cells.
item.abstract: Predictable and tuneable gene expression is essential for advanced mammalian cell engineering yet remains challenged by genomic position effects and copy number variability. This study systematically compares random integration (RI) and targeted integration (TI) of two synthetic lineariser gene circuits, TetR/eGFP_Lin and PhlFd/mCherry_Lin, in CHO-S cells. Both circuits exhibited strong linearity and orthogonality across integration strategies, but integration method and repressor choice produced distinct performance trade-offs. RI increased achievable dynamic range for PhlFd but increased basal leakiness for TetR, whereas TI, via a dual-landing-pad system, constrained copy number, and reduced basal expression and PhlFd expression variability. These findings highlight integration context and circuit architecture as key design parameters informing rational design of synthetic regulators for biopharmaceutical applications.

item.title: Photobiocatalytic Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Non-Canonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical Dyads and Triads.
item.abstract: Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C-C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of non-canonical amino acids bearing either skipped α,γ-stereo-chemical dyads or contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads. Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase β-subunit, protein engineering generated complementary enzyme variants that selectively construct three of the four possible α,γ-stereoisomers through biocatalyst-controlled reversal of both remote γ-stereochemistry and proximal α-stereochemistry. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C-C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording α,γ-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereose-lectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient β-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived amino-acrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous α,β,γ-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:<0.1:<0.1 d.r. and >99:1 e.r.. To further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this platform, the stereochemically enriched amino acids were transformed into valuable γ-chiral amines through engineered PLP-dependent tryptophan decarboxylases, establishing a dual PLP enzyme-based biocatalytic cascade for the en-antiodivergent synthesis of privileged amine scaffolds. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme-controlled γ-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates π-π interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.

item.title: A minimally modified AAV9 variant (AAV9fyhr) for enhanced CNS gene delivery by intra-CSF administration.
item.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) mediated gene therapies continue to show promise for the treatment of genetic diseases. However, delivery and safety still represent significant prohibitive barriers restricting translation of these delivery modalities to humans. We describe a novel AAV9 variant, "AAV9fyhr" or "FYHR", identified from screening a controlled randomization point mutation AAV9 library in mice and nonhuman primates followed by directed evolution of in vivo CNS-derived libraries screened in human iPSC differentiated cortical neurons. Capsid variants of interest were identified by coupling long read sequencing and computational structure modeling. Structure-function analysis of our lead candidate reveal that two targeted amino acid changes are sufficient to result in beneficial pleiotropic effects across viral stability, cell surface attachment, and gene delivery. We developed a novel multiplexed barcoding reporter system, enabling a time and cost-effective option to gather spatially resolved single cell capsid validation data in mice and nonhuman primates. When administered intrathecally, AAV9fyhr exhibits 2-to-6-fold higher gene delivery across several tissues in the CNS while minimally altering the tropism to peripheral tissues in comparison to AAV9. These findings demonstrate the potential of whole capsid engineering for the rational development of translational next generation AAV capsids.

item.title: Archival data storage using DNA proximity graphs
item.abstract: DNA offers a promising medium for long-term archival data storage, but data-specific DNA synthesis remains costly. Here we introduce SPAN (Synthesis-free Proximity-graph Archiving in Nucleic acids), a synthesis-independent storage architecture in which information is written as a physical pattern and encoded in the spatial relationships of randomly barcoded DNA molecules. Barcodes are deposited onto an optically patterned surface, and an enzymatic reaction records neighboring barcode pairs. Sequencing these pairs produces a proximity graph from which the information is decoded. We demonstrate this principle by writing a 136-bit pattern using photolithography and recovering 90% of the bits. Our cost analysis estimates lower writing costs than any existing DNA storage method. Using established commercial optical writing technologies, we project a further five-order-of-magnitude cost reduction to below flash memory costs. Although readout is more expensive, this trade-off is attractive for deep archival storage, where information is written once and rarely, if ever, retrieved.
item.authors: Perry, E.,  Tiepelt, J.,  Jacobson, J.

item.title: Nucleic acid synthesis screening at an inflection point: U.S. policy momentum and global implications.
item.abstract: This article examines the positioning of nucleic acid synthesis screening (NASS) policy within the current U.S. political landscape, tracing its evolution from voluntary industry practices to executive and legislative action across administrations. We analyze the sources of NASS's political momentum, including the rare convergence of bipartisan national security imperatives, industry support for codified screening requirements, and biosecurity-related incidents. We assess key policy challenges, including navigating jurisdictional limitations and congressional gridlock, the risk of regulatory capture, and ensuring regulatory frameworks remain adaptive to evolving technologies. We situate U.S. efforts within an international context, examining parallel initiatives in the United Kingdom, the European Union, and New Zealand, noting how U.S. market-access requirements may promote de facto global screening adoption through economic incentives rather than multilateral diplomacy. We recommend specific policy instruments, such as expanding the U.S.-based third-party screening industry, leveraging federal procurement requirements, aligning with ISO standards, and building on NIST's maturing capability-based benchmarks, to establish enforceable domestic requirements while extending global reach.

item.title: Design and validation of a GMP-compliant manufacturing platform of extracellular vesicles from mesenchymal stromal cells.
item.abstract: There is growing interest in mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) as key components in the development of next-generation regenerative cell-free therapies; however, their clinical translation remains limited by a lack of validated clinical-grade manufacturing platforms. Thus, we have established a good manufacturing practice (GMP)-compliant, semi-automated, mid-scale manufacturing workflow that couples the single-use stirred-tank bioreactor expansion of Wharton's jelly-derived MSCs with tangential flow filtration and automated size-exclusion chromatography, featuring in-line monitoring of critical process parameters. The MSC-EV-based product meets pre-specified critical quality attributes (CQAs), co-expresses parental-cell- and EV-specific markers, and complies with standardized quality and safety regulations. Moreover, the final product CQAs-including CD73-associated immunomodulatory activity-remained within acceptable limits for 12 months of storage in PlasmaLyte 148 at -80°C. Overall, our integrated platform yields MSC-EVs with high batch-to-batch reproducibility, in alignment with current GMP and regulatory standards, thereby providing a robust foundation supporting their potential clinical applicability.

item.title: Rational Tuning of Intracellular Release Kinetics in PROTAC-Peptide Conjugates via Positional Modulation of Functional Peptide Domains.
item.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) can induce degradation of otherwise challenging proteins, but their large size and unfavorable physicochemical properties often limit cellular delivery. We designed PROTAC-peptide conjugates containing a nona-arginine cell-penetrating peptide (R9), a redox-sensitive disulfide linker, and an aromatic-rich peptide sequence previously described as an endosomal escape domain (EED). The EED sequence was positioned at either the N- or C-terminus to examine how peptide-domain arrangement affects intracellular fluorescence, payload release, and BRD4 degradation. At 10 and 100 nM, the C-terminal variant MZ1-R9-EED produced a greater reduction in BRD4 abundance at 24 h than MZ1-R9 and MZ1-EED-R9, although the two-concentration comparison did not permit determination of DC50, D max, or hook effects. FAM-based flow cytometry yielded pH-sensitive cell-associated fluorescence signals that could not be interpreted as an absolute measure of total cellular uptake. Qualitative confocal microscopy showed punctate fluorescence with apparent LysoTracker overlap but did not provide quantitative evidence of endosomal escape. Under a defined cell-free reducing condition, MZ1-R9-EED underwent faster apparent disulfide cleavage, with a half-life of 0.21 h versus 0.36-0.47 h for the other conjugates, and yielded higher apparent intracellular free MZ1 levels under identical analytical conditions. Square-wave voltammetry revealed no substantial differences in reduction potential, whereas molecular dynamics simulations suggested a possible contribution of local steric accessibility. These findings associate peptide-domain positioning with cleavage kinetics, free-payload levels, and BRD4 reduction, identifying domain arrangement as a design variable for disulfide-linked PROTAC-peptide conjugates without establishing cleavage as the rate-limiting or causal mechanism.

item.title: Circulating tumor DNA in body fluids for molecular characterization of cancers beyond tissue and blood.
item.abstract: Liquid biopsy using circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is increasingly used for cancer profiling and monitoring, but blood-based analysis may not capture tumor heterogeneity across anatomical compartments. We evaluated cell-free DNA from cerebrospinal (n = 7), pleural (n = 11), pericardial (n = 1), and ascitic (n = 26) fluids from 45 patients with advanced cancer, comparing molecular findings with matched tissue, blood, and cytology where available. Oncogenic alterations were detected in 87% of body fluid samples, with a median variant allele frequency of 3.15%. TP53 (49%), EGFR (18%), and KRAS (18%) were the most frequently altered genes, and ESCAT tier IA alterations occurred in 31.1% of patients. In six patients (13.3%), potentially targetable alterations were detected in body fluids but not in blood and/or tissue. Among five cytology-negative samples, four were ctDNA positive. These findings support body fluid ctDNA profiling as a complementary approach to tissue, plasma, and cytology, thereby warranting prospective validation.

item.title: Neural Organoids and Organoid Extracellular Vesicles for Spinal Cord Injury Repair.
item.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes long-term disability in part because secondary injury progressively reshapes the lesion microenvironment and restricts axonal regeneration, circuit re-establishment, and white matter repair. Neural organoids are emerging from human pluripotent stem cell-derived disease models into implantable regenerative constructs that may provide structured cellular niches, support host-graft integration, and contribute to remyelination. However, their translation remains constrained by batch variability, limited vascularization, immune-related risk, and long-term safety concerns. In parallel, organoid-derived extracellular vesicles (OEVs) represent a cell-free modality linked to the organoid platform and are more amenable to controlled dosing and repeated administration. However, direct evidence supporting the therapeutic use of neural OEVs in SCI remains limited. OEVs should not be viewed as inherently superior alternatives to conventional extracellular vesicles (EVs); rather, their potential distinctiveness depends on experimentally verifiable links to source-organoid identity, developmental stage, multicellular context, and cargo-function logic. In SCI repair, current evidence should be stratified into direct evidence from neural OEV studies, supportive evidence from SCI-relevant conventional EV systems and related organoid/OEV studies, and testable translational hypotheses. This Review defines neural organoids and neural OEVs as source-linked but mechanistically non-equivalent repair modules, and proposes a mechanism-linked, stage-aware, and quality-oriented framework to guide OEV characterization, benchmarking, and translational evaluation for SCI repair.

item.title: Assessment of Cell-Free MicroRNA by NGS Whole Transcriptome Analysis in Cutaneous Melanoma Patients' Blood.
item.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRs) are small RNA molecules (18-22 nucleotides) that regulate the transcriptome at a post-transcriptional level by affecting the expression of specific genes. This regulatory mechanism is critical to maintain cell homeostasis and specific functions. Aberrant expression of miRs has been associated with pathobiological processes, including cancer. There are few technologies available that are able to profile whole-genome miR expression using minimal amounts of blood samples and without the need for time-consuming extraction steps. Here, we describe the HTG EdgeSeq miR Whole Transcriptome Assay (WTA) in serum and plasma samples. To identify specific cell-free miR (cfmiR) patterns, we have first focused on the analysis of normal donor samples and have then compared these to patients with cutaneous melanoma. The identification of specific cfmiR for melanoma patients will allow for better patient surveillance during targeted and/or checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (CII) treatment.

item.title: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles in cell-free therapeutics for neurological diseases.
item.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles offer a promising frontier in nanomedicine for managing neurological diseases. This review systematically addresses their classification, botanical sources, isolation techniques, and biogenesis pathways. Comprehensive compositional analyses reveal a diverse cargo of proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and metabolites that support their biological activity. Plant-derived extracellular vesicles possess intrinsic anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antineoplastic, and regenerative properties, while also serving as efficient natural drug-delivery systems. We then summarize their therapeutic applications in nervous system tumors, traumatic neurological injuries, neurodegenerative diseases, and neuropsychiatric disorders. Although substantial challenges remain in standardizing isolation protocols and optimizing targeted delivery, plant-derived extracellular vesicles offer a sustainable, highly biocompatible, and scalable alternative to mammalian-derived extracellular vesicles. Future research should focus on harnessing their unique characteristics to improve cargo engineering and facilitate transport across physiological barriers, including the blood-brain barrier. Addressing these challenges and further optimizing the functionality of plant-derived extracellular vesicles could profoundly reshape the landscape of neurological therapeutics.
